findings.title: Changes to a repair job can leave its status out of date
findings.claim: Two workshop speakers describe different coordination failures: rewriting changed job cards and abandoning updates to a shared sheet. A small shop finds a whiteboard sufficient.

evidence.quote: Two bike repairs missed pickup yesterday because we rewrote the job cards after the parts list changed.
I built a shared repair sheet, but I stopped updating it during busy shifts. An old status caused one unnecessary call.

counterevidence.quote: My small repair shop uses a whiteboard. It is enough for four bikes at a time, and I do not want another subscription.

findings.counterevidence_search: All five invented records were inspected, including the sufficient-alternative case.
findings.uncertainty: Synthetic illustration only; no inference about real users or market prevalence.
findings.segment: Repair shops with changing parts or busy shifts
findings.task: Keep the repair queue and parts approvals current
findings.consequence: One shop reports two missed pickups; another reports one unnecessary call. These are separate projects.
findings.workaround: Paper cards and a self-built shared sheet.
findings.recommendation: Test a low-effort update step before adding a detailed tracking system.
findings.next_test: Observe one busy shift and test whether staff keep status current without duplicate entry.

dimensions.name: consequence
dimensions.rationale: Reported missed pickups and avoidable call, assigned by analyst.

dimensions.name: update_feasibility
dimensions.rationale: No proposed solution has been tested.

findings.title: Parts visibility is wished for; QR codes are only advice
findings.claim: One mechanic wants customers to see approved parts before ordering. A different speaker suggests QR codes without having tried them. Neither statement establishes adoption.

evidence.quote: I wish a customer could see the approved parts list before I order anything.
You could attach a QR code to every bike. I have not tried that system in a workshop.

findings.counterevidence_search: All five invented records were inspected, including the sufficient-alternative case.
findings.uncertainty: Synthetic illustration only; no inference about real users or market prevalence.
findings.task: Confirm the parts list with a customer
findings.next_test: Check how approvals happen today and whether customers can act on a shared list.
